title: a seal records the platform it was measured on, so a green can be told from a Windows green
intention: A seal's evidence.conditions carries a platform key (sys.platform and the machine), so a record can say it was measured on Windows or Linux, and a green that replaces a red from another platform is flagged by the existing conditions notice.
why: Measured 2026-11-13 on akiendell: a validation's evidence.conditions (cairn/devices/installer validations/test_installer.json) holds the interpreter path, isolation, timeout and env digests but no platform key; akienasus found ten seals since 11-11 that name no box, so nobody can tell whether a tooth was ever green on Windows (orchestrator, 2026-11-13).
traces_to: Law 3 (a measurement says under what it was measured) and Law 9 (a green is earned on a named box).
how: In conditions.measure add "platform": f"{sys.platform} {platform.machine()}". changed() already compares any key on both sides, so a platform move notifies with no edit. Two teeth import the tester inside their body.

clauses.claim: measure() returns a platform condition equal to sys.platform and platform.machine() for a proof, where it returned none
changed() names platform when a red recorded under one platform is compared with a green recorded under another

decisions.text: D1: one key in conditions.measure; changed() is untouched.
D2: one proof, one tooth per clause; red first.

measured.saw: test_installer.json conditions keys: proof, fixtures, interpreter, isolation, timeout, env; no platform. conditions.changed() compares keys present on both sides only.
